analysis.title: Macro Derivs Flow: Equity flows more constructive than index moves would suggest
key_insights: UBS S&T (Shane Carroll, 1 Nov 2026) says hedge fund flows over the last week were more constructive than headline index moves suggest.

Early in the week HF flows were more bearish, with Hyperscalers leading the selling. Tech flows improved through the week, led by Semis. The Friday sell-off saw decent HF buy skew, including in Hyperscalers.
HFs also bought Software, mainly Quality software, and AI Industrials/Power, though the AI Industrials/Power buying was more short covering than outright buying.

The derivs desk saw decent Tech upside demand, led by Memory, mainly DRAM (Nov and Dec call spreads), and EWY ($8m premium spent on Nov calls). Most of the memory upside came Wednesday after Hynix's strong results and before Samsung's weak results.
Broader index flows flipped from hedging at the start of the week ($35m premium spent on Nov downside) to upside later in the week (SPX and QQQ call ratio structures).
Long-only flows were more defensive: selling crowded names and rotating into defensives.

Asia flows were mixed. Japan Tech saw buying after many weeks of HF degrossing. Korea was mixed (upside buying in derivs including KOSPI2 KO calls, selling in futures, flat in cash). Taiwan flows skewed to selling.
China flows were particularly weak, with continued HSTECH selling for the week. On CSI, little buying came through on the sell-off, as clients want signs of stabilisation first.

In Brazil's sell-off, equities and FX reacted differently. Equities saw initial dip-buying in cash and derivs, then two-way activity. FX saw BRL unwinds first, then fresh USDBRL downside later in the week.
The dominant FX theme remains EURUSD downside demand, including via EURBRL downside. USDCNH downside buying also persists, including via CNH correlation structures vs EUR, SGD and AUD.
Profit taking has started on USDKRW downside given how strong the KRW rally has been.

On Gold, intermediaries (including Sovereigns) have been buying at the 4k level, but broader active money Gold flows are muted. The desk feels Gold is being used as a source of funds amid the AI sell-off. The ETF desk saw strong buying in Metals ETFs, particularly GDXJ.

In rates, the clearest theme is continued demand for USD receivers across 1y, 5y and 10y tails, focused on a-30 to a-75 strikes and 3m-1y expiries. This has shifted option pricing towards the receiver side, and the desk sees little demand to fade the move.
